data.name: Fidelius
data.gender_notes: Fidelius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'fidelis', meaning 'faithful, trustworthy'. In Christian tradition, Fidelius is associated with the Roman centurion who chose to be buried with his deceased master rather than deserting him, demonstrating the ultimate expression of loyalty and faithfulness. The name Fidelius carries the meaning “Faithful, trustworthy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Fidelius usually hope their child will grow to embody faithful, trustworthy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the virtue of faithfulness, especially in the face of adversity or difficult circumstances.
data.etymology: Fidelius belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Faithful, trustworthy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fidelius total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: פידליוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פידליוס הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו במילה הלטינית Fidelius, שפירושה נאמן או נאמנות. השם קשור למושג האמונה וההתמסרות לאלוהים. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב הנוצרים כסמל לנאמנות ולמחויבות לאלוהים ולכנסייה.

in_greek.name: Φιδέλιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Φιδέλιος είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη Fidelius, που σημαίνει πιστός ή πιστότητα. Το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια της πίστης και της αφοσίωσης στο Θεό. Το όνομα χρησιμοποιείται από τους χριστιανούς ως σύμβολο πιστότητας και δέσμευσης στο Θεό και στην Εκκλησία.

in_latin.name: Fidelius
in_latin.long_meaning: Fidelius is a Christian name derived from the Latin word Fidelius, meaning faithful or loyalty. The name is connected to the concept of faith and devotion to God. The name has been used by Christians as a symbol of fidelity and commitment to God and the Church.

in_english.meaning: Faithful, loyal, and devoted to God
in_english.long_meaning: Fidelius is a Christian name originating from the Latin word Fidelius, meaning faithful or loyalty. The name is rooted in the Hebrew and Greek concepts of faith and devotion. In Christian tradition, Fidelius symbolizes commitment to God and the Church. The name conveys a sense of trust, reliability, and spiritual dedication.

data.cultural_impact: Fidelius is a name rooted in the rich history and values of Roman culture, evoking images of bravery, duty, and unwavering loyalty. It serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Roman empire and the values that continue to shape our modern world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Fidelius holds great spiritual significance, highlighting the Christian virtues of faithfulness, trustworthiness, and self-sacrifice. It serves as a reminder of the importance of keeping our promises to God and to others, and to remain faithful in our walk with Him. Furthermore, it embodies the spirit of martyrdom and the ultimate commitment to serving God above all else.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Fidelius signifies trust and faithfulness. Named after the Roman soldier who hid the Roman general's baby son Verginius, ensuring his safety during a time of political turmoil. Embodying the virtues of loyalty and dedication to one's trusted commitments.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Fidelius was a Roman centurion who protected Saint Samson of Dol from his enemies. When Samson was threatened by the pagan king Auban, Fidelius took the saint to his home and hid him in a barrel. After Auban's men searched the city and failed to find Samson, they set fire to Fidelius' house. Believing Samson to be dead, Auban's men left, and Fidelius and Samson emerged from the barrel unharmed. Fidelius then took Samson to Brittany, where they founded the monastery of Dol.
historical_references.context: Early Christian history in Rome and Brittany

historical_references.reference: Fidelius was also the name of a Roman soldier who, according to legend, was entrusted by Julius Caesar with the sacred rites of the goddess Venus. Fidelius protected the rites during Caesar's absence, but when Caesar returned, he was suspicious of Fidelius and demanded to know where the rites were kept. Fidelius, rather than betray the trust, took his own life to protect the sacred rites.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Fidelius continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
